title: Usage Insights API: route list endpoint (top spend) w/ filters, pagination, and query cost budget
creator: Logan Wright
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Build the backend API endpoint that powers the Console "Routes" list for Usage Insights. This endpoint returns the top cost drivers ranked by spend over a time window, with filters, pagination, and strict query cost controls.

Context
- Console needs a fast route list view: "Which routes are costing us the most?" and quick filtering by environment/region/deployment mode.
- Data source is the new route/model aggregates (ENG-8422). This endpoint should ONLY query pre-aggregated tables/materialized views; no raw event scans.

Primary user stories
1) As an engineer, I can see my top routes by total cost and quickly spot week-over-week changes.
2) As an ops/FinOps user, I can filter by project/environment/region to isolate cost drivers.
3) As an enterprise customer, results respect org/project boundaries and do not leak cross-project data.

API shape (proposed; align with API standards)
- GET /v1/usage-insights/routes

Query parameters
- time_start, time_end (ISO-8601; required)
- granularity: hour | day (optional; default auto: <=48h => hour, else day)
- org_id (implicit from auth), project_id (required unless caller is org-admin and explicitly sets project scope)
- environment: prod | staging | dev (optional)
- region (optional)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private (optional)
- route_prefix (optional; for client-side search-as-you-type, prefix match only)
- include_unknown_route: true|false (default true)
- sort: cost_desc | cost_asc | p95_latency_desc | error_rate_desc (default cost_desc)
- limit: 1..200 (default 50)
- cursor (opaque; returned from API)

Response fields (per route)
- route (string; normalized canonical route identifier)
- display_route (string; if we apply hashing/rollups, display what console should show)
- total_cost_usd
- input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens
- request_count
- error_rate
- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms
- cost_delta_usd (vs prior period of equal duration; optional for MVP but needed for "what changed" sparkline/delta column)
- cost_delta_pct (optional)
- model_count (optional; number of models observed for this route in the window)

Non-functional requirements
SLA / performance targets (Console-facing)
- API p95 latency: <= 300ms for typical queries (limit <= 50, day granularity, single project)
- API p99 latency: <= 800ms
- Availability: covered by Usage Insights APIs SLO doc (see Confluence)

Query cost budget / guardrails
- Must hit only aggregate tables with partition pruning by (org_id/project_id, window_start) and must have an upper bound on scanned partitions.
- Hard caps:
  - Max time window: 31 days (return 400 if exceeded)
  - Max rows returned: limit <= 200
  - If hour granularity requested for > 7 days, coerce to day granularity (return warning in response header)
- Implement statement timeout at the DB layer for this endpoint (e.g., 2s) and return a typed error code on timeout.

Caching
- Short TTL caching allowed (e.g., 30s) keyed by (org_id, project_id, filters, time window, sort, limit, cursor) to absorb dashboard refreshes.
- Must not cache across tenants; ensure cache key includes org/project.

RBAC / tenant isolation
- Must enforce org_id/project_id scoping consistent with other Console analytics endpoints.
- Explicit tests for cross-project leakage.
- Coordinate with ENG-8428 for shared authz helper / middleware.

Implementation notes
- Preferred approach: query a pre-aggregated view keyed by (org_id, project_id, route, bucket_start) and compute totals over the requested window.
- Prior-period delta: compute a second aggregate over [time_start - duration, time_start) and join on route.
  - If this is too heavy, ship without deltas behind a response flag and add in Phase 2.
- Route prefix search should remain prefix-only; do not introduce substring/regex scans.
- "Unknown route" handling: treat as a normal route value (e.g., route = "unknown") but allow exclude via include_unknown_route=false.

Error handling (typed)
- invalid_time_range
- time_range_too_large
- invalid_cursor
- query_timeout
- forbidden_scope

Acceptance criteria
- Endpoint returns stable, deterministic ordering for pagination (tie-breaker: route ascending) so cursor pagination does not skip/duplicate.
- Meets p95 latency targets on staging with representative dataset (at least 30 days of aggregates, cardinality ~50k routes/org).
- Enforces all guardrails (max range, limit, granularity coercion).
- Unit tests for filter parsing + cursor handling.
- Integration test verifying org/project scoping.
- Observability:
  - metrics: request_count, p95/p99 latency, db_query_time, cache_hit_rate, timeout_count
  - structured logs include org_id/project_id, time_range_days, limit, sort, rows_returned, query_plan_hash (if available)

References
- Confluence: API Standards Addendum "usage-insights-analytics-api-contract"
- Confluence: SLO "usage-insights-apis-slo"
- Confluence: Cardinality guardrails "cost-attribution-cardinality-guardrails"
- Linear: ENG-8422 (aggregates), ENG-8424 (route detail endpoint), ENG-8425 (export)

Open questions
- Do we require project_id for v1, or allow org-wide view for org admins? Current proposal: require project_id for v1 to reduce query cost + simplify RBAC.
- Do we include p50/p95 latency in route list v1? (Design wants it for quick triage; may be optional behind include_performance=true param.)
- Delta calculation: ship in v1 or phase 2? If included, we need to ensure it doesn’t double query time under load.

Planned work breakdown
- Implement request validation + filter normalization
- Implement DB query against aggregates + cursor pagination
- Add prior-period delta join (if feasible within budget)
- Add cache layer + invalidation semantics (TTL-based)
- Add metrics + tracing spans
- Add RBAC middleware + tests
- Load test with worst-case parameters and adjust guardrails
comments: 2026-02-10 — Paula Mendes: Please ensure the default view matches the Console design: sort by total_cost_usd desc, limit=50, and include cost deltas vs prior period for the sparkline column if possible. If deltas slip, call out in release notes as limitation.

2026-02-11 — Allison Grant (SRE): Add a hard DB statement timeout + emit a specific metric on timeout. Also please log time_range_days and whether the query was coerced from hour->day so we can correlate spikes.

2026-02-13 — Jada Williams: For cursor stability, don’t rely on floating-point cost ordering alone. Recommend ORDER BY total_cost_usd DESC, route ASC and encode both in the cursor payload (opaque to clients).

2026-02-18 — Chloe Martin: Started implementation in console-backend service. Using aggregates_daily for >48h and aggregates_hourly otherwise. Prefix search is implemented as route >= prefix AND route < prefixNext (avoids ILIKE scans). Next: delta query + integration tests for RBAC.

2026-02-21 — Nadia Rahman: Aggregates tables will have late-arriving metering updates; keep endpoint semantics as “best available within retention window” and avoid caching >60s to reduce confusion during backfills.
2026-02-23 — Logan Wright: Please align error codes with the API contract doc (query_timeout vs timeout). Also add a guardrail: if route_prefix is provided, cap limit to 100 to avoid expensive sorts.
